This comparison analyzes the 30-day mortality rates following acute surgery for patients with a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 1 or 2, serving as a supplementary indicator to indicator 9b [^src1]. The data highlights that patients with mild to moderate comorbidities (score 1-2) experience increased mortality compared to those with a score of 0, revealing significant performance variations across Danish regions and individual hospital units [^src1].

**Leaders and Trailers**
At the regional level, [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] records the highest current mortality rate at 16.9% (95% CI: 9.8-26.3), making it the worst-performing region for this indicator [^src1]. Conversely, [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] achieves the lowest mortality rate among the listed hospital units at 7.7% (95% CI: 3.1-15.2) [^src1]. The national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] stands at 12.5% (95% CI: 10.6-14.6) [^src1]. 

**Targets and Standards**
While the table's structure does not display a specific numerical threshold for a met/not-met flag, the clinical standard emphasized in the source summary is that this specific patient cohort (Charlson Score 1 or 2) inherently faces elevated mortality risks when compared to the baseline of patients with a Charlson Score of 0 [^src1]. 

**Trends Across Dated Sections**
The table provides a three-year view, allowing for trend analysis across the 2021/22, 2022/23, and current reporting periods. [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] demonstrates consistent improvement, with mortality declining steadily from 16.4% in 2021/22 to 15.4% in 2022/23, and further down to 14.2% in the current year [^src1]. In contrast, [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] shows stagnation, remaining the highest across all three periods (17.1%, 16.9%, and 16.9%) [^src1]. Nationally, [[danmark|Danmark]] saw a decrease from 13.8% in 2021/22 to 11.3% in 2022/23, before a slight rebound to 12.5% in the current year [^src1].

**Outliers**
[[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] appears as a statistical outlier due to low patient volumes, resulting in masked numerator and denominator data (`#/#`) [^src1]. This small sample size leads to high volatility in its reported rates, which swung from 12.5% in 2021/22 to 0.0% in 2022/23, and back up to 14.3% in the current year [^src1]. Additionally, [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]] showed a notable spike from 6.5% in 2021/22 to 11.6% in the current year, despite a dip to 6.5% in 2022/23 [^src1].
